page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.mn4.xlarge is a shared-core general purpose instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 4 shared vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, supported by 16.0 GB of system memory. This hardware setup establishes a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Hardware features include support for AVX, AVX-512, and AVX-512 VNNI instruction sets, along with 35 MB of L3 cache. There are no dedicated GPUs attached, no bundled local instance storage is included, and baseline network throughput is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements indicate modest computational and memory subsystem throughput consistent with shared-core resources. The instance recorded 947.0 in Geekbench single-core and 2874.0 in multi-core testing, with a PassMark CPU score of 5160.13 and stress-ng multi-core performance of 4280.62. Memory tests show write throughput of 26.2 GB/sec on large 256MB blocks, though read throughput and cached operations sit in the lower quartile of tracked cloud tiers. Data compression tasks show lower throughput, registering 19.17 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 12.32 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

Operating on shared CPU resources reduces hardware costs while delivering adequate baseline capacity for non-critical systems. However, the lack of local NVMe storage requires external network block volumes for disk I/O, and the shared CPU model introduces potential multi-tenant contention during peak utilization. The instance is suited for staging environments, development servers, lightweight backend services, internal tooling, and moderate web serving where continuous full-core execution is not required.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.mn4.xlarge is a general purpose shared-core virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz, it supplies 4 shared vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. The instance includes AVX-512 vector extensions but lacks local disk storage and GPU hardware, operating with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations place its compute and memory throughput in the entry-tier brackets, with Geekbench scores of 947.0 single-core and 2874.0 multi-core, alongside a 26.2 GB/sec memory write rate. Given its shared CPU allocation and economical resource profile, it functions effectively for development staging, lightweight microservices, internal line-of-business applications, and moderate static web traffic.
